## Defaults

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-roles.sh from each rule's strength line. Change the rule, then rebuild; do not edit this file. -->

Each line is one rule: its title, its one sentence, and the file that holds it.

- **Fail a build only for a broken Law.** A mechanical check fails a build only for a Law (a rule whose violation is a bug) or a correctness constraint it can prove; for a Default (the preferred choice, replaced when a local constraint clearly points elsewhere) it warns, for a Preference (house consistency, no architectural claim) it informs, and a Tooling rule (a replaceable implementation choice) stays easy to change. [`core/fail-a-build-only-for-a-broken-law.md`]
- **Fix the root cause, not the symptom.** Fix the boundary, model, configuration, or dependency direction that caused the problem before adding a shim (a workaround layer around it). [`coding/fix-the-root-cause-not-the-symptom.md`]
- **Prove the invariant even when a library provides the capability.** When a library provides a capability, still prove the invariant, choose the correct boundary, and understand each provider's failure model. [`coding/prove-the-invariant-even-when-a-library-provides-the-capability.md`]
- **Add a package only for commodity machinery.** Add a package for commodity machinery, and write small, fully understood product logic yourself when a package's scope, runtime cost, maintenance state, or semantic mismatch outweighs the code it would replace; every package must earn its place. [`coding/add-a-package-only-for-commodity-machinery.md`]
- **Wrap a dependency only when the wrapper adds meaning.** Do not wrap a library or a generated client one-for-one, and never merely because the code is generated; add a layer only when it combines several calls into one capability, adds non-trivial policy or orchestration, or translates an external model into the application's own terms (a translation layer) because another team owns it, it changes independently of the application, or tests need an abstraction (an interface the application owns). [`coding/wrap-a-dependency-only-when-the-wrapper-adds-meaning.md`]
- **Add an abstraction only at a real boundary.** Add an interface, port, adapter, or other indirection only where there is a real boundary: I/O, plausible variability such as a second implementation, another owner, a runtime boundary, a dependency across modules, or a test that needs it. [`coding/add-an-abstraction-only-at-a-real-boundary.md`]
- **Keep code local until it is shared.** Keep code beside its one consumer, and promote it only when it has more than one real consumer, stable enough ownership, and clearer value shared than duplicated. [`coding/keep-code-local-until-it-is-shared.md`]
- **Keep shared code with the feature that owns it.** Code used by several consumers stays with the feature that owns it, behind that feature's public entry point (on the backend, the module's published contract: the types it deliberately exposes to other modules); move it to the shared folder only when no single feature owns it. [`coding/keep-shared-code-with-the-feature-that-owns-it.md`]
- **Register dependencies explicitly.** Register and wire every dependency by name in code a reader can open; do not use assembly scanning, reflection conventions, or provider discovery. [`coding/register-dependencies-explicitly.md`]
- **Import from the file that owns the code.** Import from the file that defines a thing; do not add barrel or re-export files, and delete the old file when code moves. [`coding/import-from-the-file-that-owns-the-code.md`]
- **Use plain data and pure functions by default.** Model data as plain types and change it with pure functions; put methods on an entity only where they protect its lifecycle invariants, and do not build inheritance-heavy models. [`coding/use-plain-data-and-pure-functions-by-default.md`]
- **Extract a helper only after the pattern repeats.** Leave similar lines duplicated until the pattern has shown itself; three similar lines beat a helper extracted the first time the shape appears. [`coding/extract-a-helper-only-after-the-pattern-repeats.md`]
- **Write code that reads top to bottom.** Write a procedure as statements in the order they run, so a reader understands each line without holding an abstraction in their head. [`coding/write-code-that-reads-top-to-bottom.md`]
- **Comment only to explain why.** Write a comment only to explain why: a constraint that is not obvious, a design decision, or a real trap; never to restate what the code says, and when in doubt leave it out. [`coding/comment-only-to-explain-why.md`]
- **Model the real type of every value.** Give every value its real type: never `any`, `object`, `object?`, or `dynamic`, and `unknown` only at a boundary until the value is parsed. [`coding/model-the-real-type-of-every-value.md`]
- **Use a dictionary only for dynamic keys.** Use `Dictionary` or `Record<string, unknown>` only for data whose keys are not known at compile time; when the keys are known, use a record or a named type. [`coding/use-a-dictionary-only-for-dynamic-keys.md`]
- **Model each state explicitly in TypeScript.** Model each state a value can be in as its own case of a union, instead of optional fields read with `?.` and `??`. [`coding/model-each-state-explicitly-in-typescript.md`]
- **Declare TypeScript functions as const.** Declare a TypeScript function as a `const`. [`coding/declare-typescript-functions-as-const.md`]
- **Handle a new enum value in every consumer.** When you add an enum value, status, or type constant, find every consumer (switches, filter arrays, display logic, serialisation) and handle the new value in each, reading outside the diff. [`coding/handle-a-new-enum-value-in-every-consumer.md`]
- **Report data safety findings before style.** Review data safety and races first (a check before a write with no atomic condition in the write, find-or-create with no unique index), then style and consistency, and do not mix the two in the findings. [`coding/report-data-safety-findings-before-style.md`]
- **Fix mechanical findings without asking.** In a review that also fixes, fix mechanical findings (dead code, stale comments, missing includes, unused variables) without asking, make a design fix from the facts and the agreed rules whatever its size, and ask the user only what those cannot settle, such as removing functionality users have, in one batched question with recommendations. [`coding/fix-mechanical-findings-without-asking.md`]
- **Leave harmless redundancy out of review findings.** Do not report redundancy that helps a reader, a threshold value tuned empirically, or an assertion that could theoretically be tighter but already covers the behaviour. [`coding/leave-harmless-redundancy-out-of-review-findings.md`]
- **Enforce at the narrowest owner with enough information.** Put enforcement of an invariant in the narrowest owner that has all the information the invariant needs. [`invariants/enforce-at-the-narrowest-owner-with-enough-information.md`]
- **Add a type to enforce an invariant only when it earns its place.** While enforcing an invariant, add a new type only when it shrinks the states that can be represented, centralises a legal transition, or owns a real consistency boundary. [`invariants/add-a-type-to-enforce-an-invariant-only-when-it-earns-its-place.md`]
- **Rule out an invalid value with the smallest tool.** Rule out an invalid value with the first of these that is enough: a precise static type or discriminated union, runtime schema validation at an untrusted boundary, then a parser or value object (a type whose construction checks its input) only when it makes invalid construction impossible or removes duplicated validation. [`invariants/rule-out-an-invalid-value-with-the-smallest-tool.md`]
- **Fix a shown race with the smallest mechanism.** For a race you have shown, use the first of these that keeps the invariant: accept last-writer-wins when it violates no invariant, a database constraint for a declarative truth, one atomic conditional statement (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` or `UPDATE ... WHERE ... RETURNING`) for a state-dependent write, a version or concurrency token when writers must detect stale state, a short transaction at the appropriate isolation level when one invariant needs several writes to be atomic, a row lock when one decision spans existing rows, then an established advisory or distributed-lock library, only when no row, constraint, or atomic statement can represent what is being coordinated. [`invariants/fix-a-shown-race-with-the-smallest-mechanism.md`]
- **Use an advisory lock only for a domain identity.** Use an advisory lock only when the thing locked is a real domain identity that no row, constraint, or atomic statement can represent; it is not the way to make an operation idempotent or to suppress duplicates. [`invariants/use-an-advisory-lock-only-for-a-domain-identity.md`]
- **Design every lock's scope, timeout, and loss handling.** When you add a lock, design its name, scope, timeout, cancellation, what happens when the connection or handle is lost (the lock can be released while the work is still running), and how it is released. [`invariants/design-every-locks-scope-timeout-and-loss-handling.md`]
- **Define idempotency key meaning in the application.** The application defines what an idempotency key (a token that makes a repeated request safe to run twice) means, including its scope, fingerprint, replay policy, and expiry, and the database or an established library reserves it and arbitrates; an idempotency key is not duplicate-content detection. [`invariants/define-idempotency-key-meaning-in-the-application.md`]
- **Use a durable queue only to assign serial ownership.** Use an established durable queue only when the invariant crosses the process boundary and the domain can give one partition or consumer serial ownership of the work. [`invariants/use-a-durable-queue-only-to-assign-serial-ownership.md`]
- **Give a guarded lifecycle one pure decider.** Give an entity one decider, a pure function that answers "may this action happen now, and if not, why?" and lists the actions that are open, when all four hold: its lifecycle is a small closed set of states (an enum, or a few flags and dates that combine into one), several user actions depend on that state, the answer is needed in several use cases and on the page, and the decision is pure because facts that need I/O are loaded first and passed in. [`invariants/give-a-guarded-lifecycle-one-pure-decider.md`]
- **Use a smaller tool when no decider fits.** When one of a decider's four conditions fails (a small closed set of states, several user actions depending on it, an answer needed in several use cases and on the page, a decision that is pure once the facts that need I/O are loaded and passed in), use the smaller tool: an inline guard, plus a flag on the read model (the object the server returns for a screen) if the page needs it, for one action guarded in one place, a flag on the read model for one yes-or-no, a plain pure decision function for one decision with one or two callers and no action list, conditional writes and constraints for transitions the system drives, a closed type that mirrors an external system's states, or the database alone when it already expresses the whole rule. [`invariants/use-a-smaller-tool-when-no-decider-fits.md`]
- **Pass state and time into a decider.** A decider takes plain state and the time as arguments and does no I/O, so it reads no clock, repository, or service, and facts that need I/O are loaded first and passed in. [`invariants/pass-state-and-time-into-a-decider.md`]
- **Take date rules from the organisation's business date.** A rule that depends on the date takes the business date, "today" in the organisation's time zone, from the one clock every caller uses, not a UTC date cut from the current instant. [`invariants/take-date-rules-from-the-organisations-business-date.md`]
- **Keep the state change out of the decider.** Formalise only the decision; the state change stays a plain transform in the use case unless the transform is itself a rule. [`invariants/keep-the-state-change-out-of-the-decider.md`]
- **Pin a rule's SQL copy to the decider.** When SQL must also express a rule the decider owns, such as a list filter by derived status, keep the SQL copy and hold it to the decider with a test. [`invariants/pin-a-rules-sql-copy-to-the-decider.md`]
- **Record a module's invariants beside its code.** A module records the invariants it owns in an `INVARIANTS.md` at the module root, beside the code a change would break. [`invariants/record-a-modules-invariants-beside-its-code.md`]
- **Record only invariants a newcomer could break.** Give an invariant an entry only when a capable newcomer could break it with a reasonable-looking change; a rule a type makes unrepresentable, or a database constraint arbitrates, needs none. [`invariants/record-only-invariants-a-newcomer-could-break.md`]
- **Record only rules that are enforced and proved.** Give a rule an entry only when it is both enforced and proved; a rule that is not is not an invariant yet and gets no entry. [`invariants/record-only-rules-that-are-enforced-and-proved.md`]
- **Give every invariant entry an id and five fields.** Each entry is a heading with a stable id, unique across the repository and never renumbered once code or docs cite it, and a present-tense title, followed by `Rule`, `Why`, `Accepts`, `Owner`, and `Proof`, with no status, author, date, or tag fields and no minimum number of alternatives or consequences. [`invariants/give-every-invariant-entry-an-id-and-five-fields.md`]
- **Write an invariant as it holds now.** Write the rule as it holds now and edit the entry when it changes; history lives in version control, and the file is not a decision log. [`invariants/write-an-invariant-as-it-holds-now.md`]
- **Confirm the proof fails without the owner.** Before writing `Owner` or `Proof`, open both and confirm the proof would fail if the owner stopped enforcing the rule. [`invariants/confirm-the-proof-fails-without-the-owner.md`]
- **Record a cross-module invariant in each owner.** A rule that spans modules is recorded by each module that enforces part of it, each entry naming its own boundary and pointing at the others. [`invariants/record-a-cross-module-invariant-in-each-owner.md`]
- **Test behaviour, not call sequences.** Assert what happened (outputs, state changes, and side effects that matter), not how the code was called or the order of its internal calls, unless that order is itself the behaviour. [`tests/test-behaviour-not-call-sequences.md`]
- **Use real dependencies first, fakes second, mocks last.** Use the real dependency when it is cheap enough, a hand-written fake (a working stand-in) when the real thing is too heavy, slow, or unstable for the test, and a mock (a stand-in from a mocking library) only at a narrow, volatile boundary; do not build the test around mocks first. [`tests/use-real-dependencies-first-fakes-second-mocks-last.md`]
- **Test through the real boundary when you can.** When behaviour crosses a boundary, test it through the real wiring and the real flow rather than an isolated unit with the wiring mocked. [`tests/test-through-the-real-boundary-when-you-can.md`]
- **Match the test level to the failure risk.** Choose the test by what could go wrong: a focused unit test for a pure decision, a behaviour test through ports (the application-owned types that name capabilities) for orchestration, a real-adapter integration test (an adapter is the implementation of a port) for persistence or protocol, a host or page composition test for wiring, and a few end-to-end tests for critical journeys; follow no fixed pyramid or branch-coverage quota. [`tests/match-the-test-level-to-the-failure-risk.md`]
- **Test pure code directly.** Test a pure function (a transform, calculation, rule, validator, or mapping) directly, with no host, mount, or stand-in. [`tests/test-pure-code-directly.md`]
- **Test an adapter directly only when it has behaviour.** Test an adapter (the implementation of a port against a database, client, or SDK) directly when it is non-trivial, its mapping matters, its failure handling matters, or the external system's API is brittle; do not write tests that only restate what the ORM or SDK does. [`tests/test-an-adapter-directly-only-when-it-has-behaviour.md`]
- **Enforce module boundaries with a check that runs.** Where the code depends on module boundaries (one feature's folder under `Modules/` must not reach into another's), enforce them with a check that runs in the build or in CI, not with a document. [`tests/enforce-module-boundaries-with-a-check-that-runs.md`]
- **Give every different outcome a test.** Every materially different outcome a change introduces has evidence at the cheapest honest level; several code branches that produce one outcome do not each need a test, and covering the wiring does not cover the use case (the Application code for one operation) behind it. [`tests/give-every-different-outcome-a-test.md`]
- **Add a test only for behaviour nothing else proves.** A test earns its place by proving behaviour no other test proves, at the cheapest level that proves it. [`tests/add-a-test-only-for-behaviour-nothing-else-proves.md`]
- **Extend an existing test before writing a new one.** Extend an existing test before writing a new one for new behaviour. [`tests/extend-an-existing-test-before-writing-a-new-one.md`]
- **Delete a test your change makes redundant.** A change that makes a test redundant deletes that test in the same change. [`tests/delete-a-test-your-change-makes-redundant.md`]
- **Never pin wording, styling, or layout in a test.** Do not assert exact wording, styling, colour, or layout; assert what the user can see or do, such as a message shown or a section revealed. [`tests/never-pin-wording-styling-or-layout-in-a-test.md`]
- **Mark an unfixed gap as an expected failure.** When a test reaches a gap (a known defect) that is reported as new work rather than fixed, mark the test as an expected failure that names that work, never as a skip, so the suite goes red the day the gap is fixed, and the mark is then removed. [`tests/mark-an-unfixed-gap-as-an-expected-failure.md`]
- **Count a fake as coverage only above the port.** A test that uses a fake or a mock covers the behaviour above the port, never the adapter it replaced; prove arbitration, atomicity, ordering, redelivery, and lock loss through the real adapter. [`tests/count-a-fake-as-coverage-only-above-the-port.md`]
- **Run one behaviour suite against fake and real adapter.** Where a fake could drift from the real adapter (the implementation of a port), run one suite of the behaviour callers rely on against the fake and against every real adapter. [`tests/run-one-behaviour-suite-against-fake-and-real-adapter.md`]
- **Type a stand-in response against the generated API types.** Type a stand-in API response against the generated API types, with `satisfies components["schemas"]["…"]` or a typed fixture helper, so a change to the API breaks the test at compile time. [`tests/type-a-stand-in-response-against-the-generated-api-types.md`]
- **Reach a fake's failures through trigger values.** In an end-to-end journey, reach a fake's failure modes through agreed trigger values in the fake, not by intercepting the page's requests. [`tests/reach-a-fakes-failures-through-trigger-values.md`]
- **Keep end-to-end journeys simple and stable.** Keep each end-to-end journey simple and happy-path first, with role or test-id selectors, no sleeps, and no state shared between tests. [`tests/keep-end-to-end-journeys-simple-and-stable.md`]
- **Coordinate concurrency tests without sleeps.** Drive the actors in a concurrency test in a fixed order with barriers, hooks, or controlled transactions, never with timing sleeps. [`tests/coordinate-concurrency-tests-without-sleeps.md`]
- **Assert the durable outcome of a race.** A concurrency test runs at the boundary that really arbitrates (the database, queue, or workflow engine that decides the winner) and asserts the durable result for the winner, the loser, any retry, and the conflict, not that a lock, repository, or queue method was called. [`tests/assert-the-durable-outcome-of-a-race.md`]
- **Judge test code by the testing rules only.** Test code may import whatever it needs and is judged by the testing rules (double names, mock density, location), not by the production rules on layer purity, module shape, or .NET style. [`tests/judge-test-code-by-the-testing-rules-only.md`]
- **Test frontend logic, composables, and pages before components.** On the frontend, test pure `logic/` directly, composables where state or orchestration matters, and pages where wiring matters, rather than making presentational components the main test surface. [`tests/test-frontend-logic-composables-and-pages-before-components.md`]
- **Test what the user can do in a UI.** Test a user interface by what the user can accomplish and understand (prerequisites and ordering, the common path, what is revealed, visible outcomes and previews, consequences, and validation and recovery guidance), not by its control layout or implementation terms. [`tests/test-what-the-user-can-do-in-a-ui.md`]
